architecture_principles: a discovered material regularity is only usable inside the chemistry family in which it was measured
a scientific applicability boundary is executable code, not prompt advice
the language model may criticize the rule and may not override it
value of information is computed by a deterministic tool over the admissible set only
held-out result data are structurally removed before any payload is assembled
every gate decision carries a machine-readable reason and is serialized with the run

arm_difference_declaration.forbidden_confound: Hiding applicability information from V5_NO_GATE while showing it to V5_FULL is prohibited by protocol v1.1.
held_identical: model endpoint and stage model assignment
evidence access profile and filtered evidence state
raw assess_shared_shape_applicability outputs for every candidate
the full inadmissible-card list and its machine-readable reasons
VOI implementation, weights and tie epsilon
arm_difference_declaration.information_parity_evidence: build_pre_enforcement_payload() takes no arm argument, and its SHA-256 is written into every run as pre_enforcement_payload_sha256. The two arms must report the same hash.
arm_difference_declaration.only_intended_difference: whether the identical chemistry-domain applicability audit is enforced as hard experiment-card admissibility before VOI and at freeze
arm_difference_declaration.payload_consequence: Both arms receive the same audit, the same per-candidate applicability outputs and the same inadmissible-card list. V5_NO_GATE marks the audit advisory and keeps every card selectable; V5_FULL marks it binding and removes the inadmissible cards from the ranked set.

candidate_space.rationale: V5 reuses the byte-identical V3/V4 lattice so that the measured change is the chemistry-domain constraint, not the search space.

architecture.canonical_flow: planner(intent + failure mode) -> mandatory chemistry-audited local science tool -> deterministic chemistry-domain applicability audit (identical and model-visible in both arms) -> enforcement (V5_FULL only) -> VOI over the selectable set -> proposer -> skeptic -> robustness adjudicator -> judge -> freeze

rules: M-HOLD-120 is admissible: it measures thermal-hold drift directly and does not use the shared thermal-response shape.
M-REPEAT is admissible: it measures realization/state spread directly.
M-SWEEP is admissible: it is the direct verification measurement for a chemistry-shifted candidate.

M-ANCHOR is admissible only when assess_shared_shape_applicability returns shared_shape_use equal to allowed_with_state_anchor, or when configs/verified_shape_transfer.json records a completed direct sweep for the same chemistry family.
Otherwise M-ANCHOR is inadmissible_before_shape_verification. This is deterministic inadmissibility, not a VOI penalty and not prompt advice.

architecture.claim_boundary: V5.0.0 selects an experiment from pre-result evidence under an outcome-blind runtime with a deterministic chemistry-domain admissibility constraint. A V5 result is evidence about executable scientific constraints on measurement choice. It is not a wet-lab result and does not claim that the historical decision used this ranking.
architecture.manuscript_boundary: V5 run results must not be written into manuscript/MAIN_TEXT_V5.md or manuscript/SUPPLEMENTARY_INFORMATION_V5.md until the run series is audited and explicitly frozen by the author.
architecture.name: PUR_NEW_CHEMISTRY_GATED_EXPERIMENT_SELECTION_AGENT_V5
non_goals: adding a language model to compute value of information or admissibility
adding Agent roles beyond planner, tools, proposer, skeptic, robustness adjudicator, judge and freeze
re-running, rewriting or reinterpreting the frozen V4 series

primary_arms.role: advice-only control isolating the incremental effect of turning identical scientific applicability information into an executable hard constraint
prospective chemistry-aware Agent V5 with executable scientific constraints

architecture.purpose: Test whether an experimentally discovered material regularity and its chemistry-domain boundary can be executed as a hard scientific constraint on which measurement an outcome-blind Agent is allowed to select.

stages.role: identify the physical failure mode and the scientific question the next experiment must answer, and request the evidence needed to judge experiments rather than formulations
execute read-only scientific tools. The chemistry-audited local rheology summary is mandatory and is forced into the trace whether or not the planner requested it.

deterministic, non-LLM measurement-applicability audit. Computed once per run without reference to the arm, fully visible to the model in both arms, serialized in full, and never produced by a model stage.
V5_FULL only. Converts the identical audit into hard admissibility before VOI ranking and again at freeze. It cannot be overridden by any model stage.
propose the experiment with the highest scientific information value from the cards present in the payload
attack the proposed experiment on hypothesis coverage, confounding, interpretability and whether its falsification criterion can actually be met
adjudicate whether the proposed experiment survives the reported weight sensitivity and the strongest objection
commit to one experiment card present in the payload, or abstain, and state its acceptance and falsification criteria
programmatically validate and freeze the experiment card. A selection outside the admissible set is rejected at freeze rather than repaired.

architecture.supersedes_nothing: V5 is a new prospective runtime. configs/agent_v4.json, scripts/run_agent_v4.py, prompts/agent_v4_*.txt, src/pur_new/voi.py and every frozen V3/V4 run record remain unchanged and are not reinterpreted by V5.

voi_tool.explicitly_not: distance to any held-out formulation. No target coordinate enters any component, weight or tie-break.
voi_tool.formula: VOI = w_hyp * hypothesis_discrimination + w_unc * uncertainty_reduction + w_dec * decision_relevance + w_int * measurement_interpretability - w_ext * extrapolation_risk - w_proc * process_state_risk
voi_tool.name: score_experiment_cards

decision_stability_sent_to_model.evaluated_over: the selectable experiment cards of this arm
decision_stability_sent_to_model.metric_is_not: model confidence; posterior probability; calibrated expected information
decision_stability_sent_to_model.voi_formula: VOI = w_hyp * hypothesis_discrimination + w_unc * uncertainty_reduction + w_dec * decision_relevance + w_int * measurement_interpretability - w_ext * extrapolation_risk - w_proc * process_state_risk. Every component is normalized to [0, 1] by construction. This is a transparent normalized score with reported weight sensitivity, not a Bayesian posterior.

evidence_policy.description: For prospective/blind Agent evaluation. The Agent may see original-system measurements and external analogue evidence, but not the target validation formulation identity, its wet-lab outcome, or any outcome-derived labels.

judge_normalized.acceptance_criterion: Accept the E1-derived parent-drift transfer used by H-CORE if every valid independent repeat has SI_15_60 between 7.51% and 11.51%, inclusive; this is the 9.51% E1 reference within the declared 2.00-percentage-point resolution.
judge_normalized.chemistry_support_statement: S1C01 is within the measured unmodified PPG2000/PDP70/MDI chemistry family. The primary observable is measured directly and does not depend on the shared temperature-response regularity, even though that regularity was measured in the same chemistry family. Therefore the result supports only the formulation-level 120 C hold-drift comparator and not a molecular mechanism or an 80-130 C response claim.
judge_normalized.falsification_criterion: If every valid independent repeat has SI_15_60 below 7.51%, the registered H-CORE numerical prediction at reactive mass fraction 1.000 is falsified beyond the 2.00-percentage-point resolution. If every repeat is above 11.51%, the E1-to-E2 numerical baseline transfer is falsified, although the qualitative linear-dilution form of H-CORE is not. Mixed repeat outcomes or values spanning either boundary are inconclusive and falsify none of H-CORE, H-RESIN, or H-DUAL.
judge_normalized.next_experiment_if_falsified: Run S1C41::M-HOLD-120 under matched preparation and thermal history, using the measured S1C01 parent-core drift as the contemporaneous dilution comparator rather than the E1-derived 7.61% value; an acrylic-only hold is subsequently required to separate H-RESIN from H-DUAL.
judge_normalized.primary_observable: Repeat-level SI_15_60 = 100 * (eta_60 - eta_15) / eta_15 at 120 C, with the arithmetic mean reported across at least two independent preparations.
judge_normalized.rationale: A contemporaneous unmodified-core hold is the most defensible first experiment because it removes the principal reference-state ambiguity that compromises interpretation of every modified-candidate hold. M-HOLD-120 directly measures the least-resolved failure coordinate without shared-shape transfer or model reconstruction. The result can validate or reject the E1-derived H-CORE baseline, but it cannot by itself distinguish H-RESIN from H-DUAL or establish any molecular mechanism.
judge_normalized.stage_disagreements_resolved: I followed the Skeptic and Robustness Adjudicator rather than the Proposer and deterministic VOI ranking. The proposed S1C41 hold directly measures the failure mode and is chemistry-admissible, but its 7.61% comparator is derived from E1 while its reactive core is E2-derived; without an E2-core hold baseline, a low modified-formulation drift cannot be cleanly attributed to modifier-associated suppression. S1C01 therefore takes priority as a state-control experiment despite lower ranked VOI. The remaining ambiguity about exact S1C01-to-E2 identity is retained explicitly rather than silently averaged away.

uncertainty_decomposition.evidence_coverage_uncertainty: Only E1 and E5 have original 120 C hold trajectories, each without independent repeats; no direct E2-core hold baseline is available. This experiment fills that specific gap but does not test modifier suppression.
uncertainty_decomposition.extrapolation_uncertainty: There is no new-chemistry extrapolation because S1C01 is unmodified and inside the measured family. Residual uncertainty comes from transferring the E1 drift coefficient across formulation differences to the E2-derived core and from the payload not explicitly mapping which of S1C01-S1C09 is the exact nominal E2 realization.
uncertainty_decomposition.measurement_uncertainty: The declared discrimination resolution is 2.00 percentage points in SI_15_60. At least two independent repeats are required, and discordant repeats are classified as inconclusive rather than adjudicated by an outcome-chosen aggregate.
uncertainty_decomposition.realization_state_uncertainty: E2 showed approximately 2.80-3.57-fold between-preparation absolute-viscosity spread. Relative drift may reduce scale sensitivity but does not remove preparation-history risk, so preparation and thermal histories must be matched and recorded.

planner.chemistry_support_statement: The local thermal-response regularities were measured in the original E-series reactive PUR chemistry, primarily E1–E3, with a separate verified E1 +P perturbation; the candidate space retains the E2 reactive core but introduces acrylic-like and/or minor tackifier-like modifiers. An experiment using those modifiers is not strictly inside the directly measured composition chemistry, so shared-shape transfer cannot be assumed until the audited chemistry boundary and candidate-specific applicability are checked. The hold comparison itself can remain anchored to the E2-core PUR family, but modified candidates require direct temperature-sweep verification if applicability is not established.
planner.failure_mode: Viscosity growth during prolonged 120 °C melt residence, with formulation-dependent thermal-hold drift that is not yet mechanistically resolved.
planner.failure_mode_evidence: The original E5 thermal hold increased by 51.54% from 15 to 60 min and by 93.08% from 15 to 90 min at 120 °C; even the least-drifting original reference, E1, increased by 9.51% from 15 to 60 min.
planner.least_resolved_justification: The local isothermal evidence consists of only one measured 120 °C hold trajectory each for E1 and E5, with four points over 15–90 min. In contrast, temperature response was measured at six temperatures from 80 to 130 °C across multiple E1–E3 runs, and realized viscosity variability was directly characterized for E2 with three runs at each temperature. The sparse, unrepeated hold data therefore provide the weakest resolution of the coordinate directly associated with the failure mode.
measurement_requirements: Measure the primary failure coordinate with M-HOLD-120: hold at 120 °C, record viscosity at 15, 30, 45, and 60 min, and report SI_15_60 = (eta_60 - eta_15) / eta_15 as a percentage.

Use at least two independent hold repeats per tested composition and retain individual trajectories so the 2 percentage-point discrimination threshold can be judged rather than silently averaging away realization variability.
Include matched reactive-mass-fraction comparisons that permit direct evaluation against the frozen H-CORE linear-dilution prediction based on the E1 15–60 min drift.

Include an acrylic-like-only condition and a condition with a nonzero minor tackifier-like fraction at an otherwise controlled design state so that tackifier necessity under H-DUAL can be distinguished from general resin suppression under H-RESIN.

Classify drift below half of the linear-dilution prediction as the registered superlinear-suppression regime, while treating predictions or observations separated by less than the declared 2 percentage-point resolution as non-separable.

Measure and report absolute viscosity at the hold sampling times, preserving the source unit as unknown if it remains unverified, so drift improvement is not accepted at an unusable realized viscosity level.

Because resin modifiers change chemistry, perform an 80–130 °C sweep in 10 °C increments unless candidate-specific shared-shape applicability is established; do not substitute an unsupported one-point calibration.

Control and record preparation and thermal history. If realized-state uncertainty remains comparable to the observed E2 spread of approximately 2.80–3.57-fold, use at least three independently prepared samples with matched temperature sweeps to separate formulation effects from process-state displacement.
planner.scientific_question: At matched reactive mass fraction and matched 120 °C residence window, does resin modification reduce viscosity drift only in proportion to reactive-core dilution, suppress it to less than half of that linear-dilution prediction, or require a nonzero minor tackifier-like fraction rather than acrylic-like modification alone? These outcomes separate H-CORE, H-RESIN, and H-DUAL.

proposer.chemistry_support_assessment: S1C41 is outside the chemistry family in which the shared temperature-response shape was measured, but M-HOLD-120 directly observes drift and does not use that shape or any model-based reconstruction. The chemistry audit therefore identifies this measurement as admissible and scientifically interpretable for the resin-modified candidate, while absolute viscosities and preparation histories should be retained because realization-state risk remains moderate.

outcome_interpretation.if_acceptance_criterion_met: If SI_15_60 remains below 3.80% across at least two repeats, drift is less than half the H-CORE linear-dilution prediction of 7.61%. This falsifies H-CORE at the registered low-drift boundary and supports superlinear resin-associated suppression, but it does not distinguish H-RESIN from H-DUAL because both predict the same low-drift outcome when both modifier axes are active.
outcome_interpretation.if_falsification_criterion_met: If SI_15_60 is at or above 7.61%, H-RESIN is falsified and the result is consistent with H-CORE's linear-dilution prediction rather than superlinear suppression. This experiment still cannot perform the registered H-RESIN versus H-DUAL test, which requires an acrylic-only hold condition.
outcome_interpretation.if_intermediate: A result between 3.80% and 7.61% indicates partial suppression that meets neither the registered superlinear-suppression acceptance boundary nor the H-RESIN falsification boundary. Values within the 2 percentage-point measurement resolution of 7.61% are not separable from H-CORE; otherwise the result suggests an effect weaker than the registered H-RESIN/H-DUAL low-drift prediction.

proposer.primary_observable: SI_15_60 = (eta_60 - eta_15) / eta_15, percent, measured directly during a 120 C hold from the 15 and 60 min viscosity readings across at least two independent repeats

ranked_alternatives.why_lower_value: VOI-tied and equally discriminating, but its 17.5 wt% acrylic loading imposes a larger chemistry perturbation than S1C41 without added hypothesis separation.
VOI-tied and directly supported at 20 wt% acrylic, but it uses more total modifier than the minimum sufficient tied card and provides no additional discrimination.
VOI-tied, but its 22.5 wt% acrylic loading is a larger departure from the local chemistry with no gain in observable directness or separated hypothesis pairs.
VOI-tied and inside the broad external support region, but its 25 wt% acrylic loading is the largest perturbation in the tied set and lies outside the conservative 15-20 wt% initial-test band.

It has the same direct drift measurement and hypothesis discrimination, but 7.5 wt% tackifier lies above the repeatedly supported 4.8-6.4 wt% cluster, creating nonzero extrapolation risk and a lower VOI score.

proposer.reasoning: M-HOLD-120 directly measures the least-resolved coordinate and declared failure mode without a model fit. S1C41 separates H-CORE from both low-drift alternatives using the preregistered 7.61% linear prediction and 3.80% superlinear threshold, stays inside the externally supported regions for both modifier axes, and minimizes modifier burden among the five genuinely tied top cards. Its limitation is explicit: because both axes are active, it cannot distinguish general resin suppression from tackifier-required suppression.
proposer.tie_break_justification: All five cards have identical VOI components and separate the same two registered hypothesis pairs. S1C41 uses the smallest modifier burden in the tied set: 15 wt% acrylic-like modifier is within the conservative initial test band, and 5 wt% minor tackifier lies in the repeatedly supported 4.8-6.4 wt% cluster. It therefore makes the smallest justified departure from the characterized reactive chemistry while retaining full coverage of both modifier axes.

robustness_adjudication.change_from_proposal: Replace S1C41::M-HOLD-120 with an unmodified E2-core M-HOLD-120 experiment to obtain the missing contemporaneous parent-core drift baseline. The chemistry-domain audit does not invalidate S1C41's direct hold observable, but the missing E2 baseline prevents clean attribution of deviation from the E1-derived 7.61% comparator. After establishing the baseline, S1C41 and an acrylic-only card such as S1C49 should be compared under matched preparation and hold conditions.
residual_decision_risk: The payload identifies S1C01-S1C09 as unmodified candidates but does not explicitly map which identifier is the exact nominal E2 realization; that identity should be verified before preparation.
An unmodified-core hold establishes the parent comparator but does not itself test modifier suppression or distinguish H-RESIN from H-DUAL.
Large E2 realization-state variability remains a confounder, so independent repeats and tightly recorded preparation and thermal histories are required.
Repeat aggregation and boundary adjudication remain underspecified; point estimates within the declared 2-percentage-point resolution interval should not be treated as hypothesis-separating.
Modifier reactivity is unverified, so later modified-formulation results cannot assume AC1920 or TK100 is chemically inert without material-functionality evidence.
M-HOLD-120 supports only the direct 120 C drift observable; claims about 80-130 C thermal-response transfer require a candidate-specific M-SWEEP.
robustness_adjudication.skeptic_objection_reasoning: The strongest objection undermines the main interpretation promised for S1C41: its 7.61% H-CORE comparator is derived from E1 even though the candidate retains an E2-derived core with different NCO:OH and MDI fraction and no measured E2 hold baseline. A low S1C41 drift could therefore reflect an E1-to-E2 core difference rather than modifier-associated superlinear suppression. The first experiment should instead directly measure the unmodified E2-core hold behavior. S1C01::M-HOLD-120 is selected from the supplied unmodified E2-core candidate group S1C01-S1C09. This scientifically justified departure from the score resolves the missing parent-core comparator before testing modified cards. The tied dual-axis cards do not solve this issue and all leave H-RESIN versus H-DUAL entangled. An acrylic-only hold such as S1C49::M-HOLD-120 remains the subsequent experiment needed to challenge tackifier necessity.
robustness_adjudication.weight_sensitivity_assessment: The proposed S1C41::M-HOLD-120 is one of five cards in the deterministic tied top set. The tied top set has top_experiment_set_stability 1.0 across all 25 single-term perturbations from 0.5x to 1.5x, and every recommendation_flip_boundary reports survival across the entire sweep. The base_margin_to_first_strictly_lower is 0.004583. Thus none of the tested perturbations changes the tied top set; no alternative weighting within the reported range requires defense. This robustness does not address the scientific validity of the E1-derived comparator.

skeptic.chemistry_domain_support_assessment: The S1C41 composition is outside the previously measured unmodified chemistry family, but the primary M-HOLD-120 observable is measured directly in S1C41 and does not reuse the unsupported shared thermal-response shape. A candidate-specific M-SWEEP is required before making claims about shape transfer or viscosity across 80-130 C; it is not required merely to read SI_15_60 at 120 C.
skeptic.falsification_criterion_assessment: M-HOLD-120 directly measures values that can be at or above 7.61%, so the criterion is operationally attainable. It is not adequately resolution-qualified: values within 2.00 percentage points of 7.61% should be declared non-separable, and the protocol must specify whether falsification requires every repeat, a prespecified aggregate, or an uncertainty bound to clear the threshold.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: A result below 3.80% would reject the registered E1-scaled numerical rule, but would not cleanly establish that S1C41 suppresses drift beyond dilution relative to its actual E2 reactive core.
objections.objection: The claimed H-CORE prediction of 7.61% is calculated as the E1 drift of 9.51% times S1C41's reactive mass fraction of 0.8000, but S1C41 preserves the E2 reactive core. E1 has NCO:OH = 1.70 and MDI fraction 0.19287, whereas E2 has NCO:OH = 1.80 and MDI fraction 0.20191. No E2 120 C hold baseline is available. Consequently, deviation from 7.61% can reflect the unmeasured E2-core drift rather than superlinear suppression by the modifiers. The numerical H-CORE versus low-drift separation is 3.804 percentage points, which exceeds the declared 2.00-point resolution, and H-RESIN versus H-DUAL is correctly declared unseparated.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: Low drift could only be called dual-modifier-associated suppression. It could not be attributed specifically to AC1920, TK100, tackifier necessity, an AC1920-TK100 interaction, reduced encounter frequency, or unchanged reactive stoichiometry.
objections.objection: S1C41 simultaneously introduces 15 wt% AC1920, 5 wt% TK100, and reduces the E2-derived reactive core to 80 wt%. Thus acrylic-like modification, tackifier-like modification, their interaction, and reactive-core dilution all change in one formulation. The linear-dilution comparison partially accounts for total reactive mass fraction, but it does not isolate the two modifier axes or verify that AC1920 and TK100 are chemically inert. The E2 stoichiometry note explicitly requires recalculation if a modifier contributes reactive OH or another NCO-reactive group, and no verified modifier functionality is supplied.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: The measured observable remains interpretable, but a case with one repeat above and one below a boundary could be adjudicated after seeing the data.
objections.objection: The primary observable itself survives this attack: SI_15_60 is calculated directly from the measured 15 and 60 min viscosities and requires no fit, extrapolation, shared thermal shape, or imputation. However, the decision rule is not fully specified for discordant repeats: acceptance says the value must remain below 3.80% across at least two repeats, while the falsification wording does not state whether every repeat, the mean, or an uncertainty bound must be at or above 7.61%.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: The direct 120 C drift result remains valid, but temperature-response transferability or viscosity usability across 80-130 C would be unsupported.
objections.objection: S1C41 is an unvalidated resin-modified AC1920+TK100 chemistry, but the selected M-HOLD-120 protocol does not reuse the shared temperature-response shape measured in unmodified PPG2000/PDP70/MDI material. Therefore the primary drift observable does not improperly transfer that shape. The proposal would exceed support only if it used the hold data or retained absolute viscosities to claim an 80-130 C response without the candidate-specific M-SWEEP recommended by the audit.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: H-RESIN could be declared falsified by a point estimate that the protocol's own resolution rule treats as indistinguishable from the boundary.
objections.objection: The protocol can physically produce SI_15_60 values at or above 7.61%, so the stated H-RESIN falsification outcome is attainable. Nevertheless, the point boundary is inconsistent with the declared 2.00-percentage-point discrimination resolution: an observed value just above 7.61% is not resolution-separated from a value just below it. The proposer partly acknowledges this by saying values within 2 points of 7.61% are non-separable from H-CORE, but the formal falsification criterion still says any value at or above 7.61% falsifies H-RESIN. Repeat-level adjudication is also unspecified.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: A direct viscosity trajectory could be presented as evidence for a specific molecular mechanism that was never measured.
objections.objection: No target hold result or validation-formulation identity is visibly used, and the payload explicitly states that exact validation coordinates and outcomes were excluded, so no concrete outcome leakage is established. Scope is still limited: M-HOLD-120 can demonstrate phenomenological drift suppression, but it cannot establish H-RESIN's stated explanation involving lower effective concentration and encounter frequency of reaction-capable species. The proposal appropriately uses the narrower phrase 'resin-associated suppression,' but any stronger molecular or encounter-frequency claim would exceed the rheological measurement.

skeptic.recommended_change: Add a contemporaneous M-HOLD-120 measurement of the unmodified E2 reactive core using the corresponding reactive-core-only card among S1C01-S1C09, after verifying which card is the exact E2 composition, so the dilution prediction is anchored to the actual parent core. Also add an acrylic-only hold card such as S1C49::M-HOLD-120 at reactive mass fraction 0.8000 to challenge H-DUAL, while explicitly acknowledging that S1C49 substitutes 20 wt% acrylic for S1C41's 15 wt% acrylic plus 5 wt% tackifier and therefore is not a pure tackifier toggle. Prespecify repeat aggregation and require the relevant uncertainty or resolution interval, rather than only the point estimate, to clear each decision boundary.
skeptic.strongest_objection: The 7.61% H-CORE comparator is transferred from E1 even though S1C41 uses an E2-derived reactive core with different NCO:OH and composition and no measured E2 hold baseline. This makes deviation from 7.61% ambiguous between modifier suppression and an unmeasured E1-to-E2 core difference.

tool_trace.reason: This mandatory upstream audit must be loaded before candidate or experiment ranking; it establishes the chemistry provenance, same-order comparisons, state-shift evidence, hold contrast, and the validated boundary of the shared thermal-response regularity.

claim_boundaries: The shared-shape/state-shift structure is established only within the measured local chemistry family.
The apparent E_eta descriptor is rheological, not a chemical reaction activation energy.
The E1/E5 hold contrast does not identify a unique molecular mechanism.
The verified E1 +P phosphoric-acid perturbation is excluded from the primary same-composition fit and is interpreted separately as a chemical-perturbation check.
No validation-formulation identity or outcome is used by this tool.
design_rules: Represent a candidate as formulation plus process/realization state, not composition alone.

Use one state-specific anchor measurement to locate a new realization or nearby local formulation on the transferable thermal-response shape when it remains inside the supported local chemistry family.
Treat static viscosity, temperature response and thermal-hold stability as separate decision variables.
When the failure mode is hot-hold drift, choose an experiment and measurement window that directly test drift rather than only matching one nominal viscosity value.
Use external resin/tackifier evidence to define chemically plausible directions, but do not convert analogue proximity into a predicted local outcome.
Keep deliberately chemistry-perturbed curves outside same-composition fitting, but use them to test whether an intervention shifts viscosity scale, thermal-response shape, or both.

chemical_perturbation_check.interpretation: The verified low-dose H3PO4 perturbation shifts the observed viscosity level while remaining closely compatible with the local shared thermal-response geometry. It is a separate chemical-perturbation check and is not pooled into the primary same-composition state model.

observational_E1_R01_day1_comparator.interpretation_boundary: Observational reference only; the compact record does not establish a paired parent-batch relationship between E1 +P and E1 R01 day-1.

one_point_state_calibration.interpretation: Within the tested local chemistry family, one state-specific viscosity anchor can locate a previously held-out nominal formulation on the shared thermal-response shape to roughly 6-10% pooled multiplicative error.
one_point_state_calibration.validation_scheme: leave one nominal formulation out; fit shared shape on the remaining formulations; use one anchor from the held formulation

state_shift_master_curve.interpretation: Within the chemistry-audited local family, a realization-specific viscosity-scale intercept plus a shared quadratic inverse-temperature response closes the data far better than a formulation-level intercept using the same thermal basis.

temporal_stability_coordinate.interpretation: Original E1 and E5 hold trajectories show that thermal-hold viscosity drift is strongly formulation dependent and should be treated separately from static viscosity.

thermal_coordinate.interpretation: The apparent temperature-sensitivity descriptor remains comparatively concentrated after chemistry auditing; it is a rheological descriptor, not a molecular reaction activation energy.

experiment_design_implications.hold_window: For the current local study, 120 C and the common 15-60 min window directly interrogate the observed instability while matching the available validation window.
experiment_design_implications.selection_target: Select a formulation-process point that is informative about the observed instability and state uncertainty, not merely the closest static-viscosity value.
experiment_design_implications.state_anchor: A single in-range anchor can be used for efficient local curve calibration; 120 C is operationally attractive because it is also the hold-stability test temperature.
experiment_design_implications.verified_acid_perturbation: E1 +P received 0.025 mmol H3PO4 from a 0.1 mol/L standard solution during dehydration. Its close agreement with the primary shared thermal shape makes it useful as a defined scale-versus-shape perturbation check, not as another nominal E1 realization.

provenance_audit.reason: E1 +P is a verified chemical perturbation: 0.025 mmol H3PO4 from a 0.1 mol/L standard solution was added during dehydration. It is excluded from the same-composition primary state model and exposed separately as a perturbation check.

experiment_intents.causal_isolation: Use when the primary objective is attribution of one formulation axis. Prefer a single active modifier axis only in this mode.
experiment_intents.performance_mitigation: Use when a measured failure mode is already established and the next experiment is intended to reduce that failure. Independently supported multi-modifier interventions are admissible.
experiment_intents.uncertainty_resolution: Use when missing process, stoichiometric or evidence information prevents an interpretable performance test.

decision_policy.purpose: Select an experimentally informative intervention from pre-result evidence without treating a literature composition as the hidden optimum.
ranking_rules: Exact distance to an external analogue anchor is audit metadata, not a primary optimization objective.
Candidates in the same evidence-support class are not rewarded merely for being numerically closer to a literature percentage.
For performance mitigation, two modifier axes may be combined when each is independently supported and the combination stays inside bounded evidence regions.

Among candidates with comparable evidence coverage and interpretability, prefer the smallest sufficient total modifier burden and the smallest justified departure from the characterized local chemistry.
A single-variable design is preferred only when causal attribution is the stated experiment intent; it is not a universal default.
Held-out validation coordinates and outcomes must never enter candidate construction, ranking or tie-breaking.

rule_text: Scope: measurement admissibility, not formulation admissibility.
M-HOLD-120, M-REPEAT and M-SWEEP observe their quantity directly and remain admissible.

M-ANCHOR is admissible only when assess_shared_shape_applicability returns shared_shape_use == 'allowed_with_state_anchor', or when a versioned prior direct sweep has verified transferability for the same chemistry family.
Otherwise M-ANCHOR is inadmissible_before_shape_verification: the one-point anchor would reconstruct 120-130 C viscosity through a shape that has never been measured for that chemistry.
This audit is a deterministic scientific rule, not a VOI penalty and not a model opinion. Whether it is binding in this run is stated by the enforcement field.

voi.formula: VOI = w_hyp * hypothesis_discrimination + w_unc * uncertainty_reduction + w_dec * decision_relevance + w_int * measurement_interpretability - w_ext * extrapolation_risk - w_proc * process_state_risk. Every component is normalized to [0, 1] by construction. This is a transparent normalized score with reported weight sensitivity, not a Bayesian posterior.
voi.tie_note: These experiments share an identical component vector. The deterministic tool is indifferent among them. Any choice within this set must be justified scientifically.
